title: The 1974 Carnegie Hall Harlem bands concert
summary: George Wein's show had Hawkins as the only leader and he did his own tunes.

blocks.x: You had, also that 1974 Carnegie Hall appearance. You know, where you were questing with Sy Oliver's band?
That was the, George Weins put that show on.
Was that music of the Harlem bands of the thirties?

Right. That's what it was. Chick Webb, they had certain tunes from different bands. I think they did one or two from Lunceford, Chick Webb, Lucky Millinder, I believe, and then they, I was about the only one leading there — is there another band there too? I was the only leader that was there to perform with my tunes, you know. So, they had all this in a

medley. They played theirs first, and then they brought me out to do the, do my own, my tunes. I think I did, was that "Uptown Shuffle"? I think I did "Uptown Shuffle". I think they had an arrangement on "After Hours", "Tippin' In", I believe, and "Tuxedo".
